claim.pdf_says: Page 1018 (printed 988) ends with "Psalter_Pahlavi:\n10B80-10B91" and nothing further. "Rejang:" is the FIRST line printed on page 1019 (printed 989), directly above "A930-A946".
claim.markdown_says: End of the page-1018 block: "Psalter_Pahlavi:\n10B80-10B91 Rejang:" - with "Rejang:" glued to the end of Psalter_Pahlavi's range line. The page-1019 block then opens with a headless "A930-A946".
claim.why_it_matters: Same normative-annex structural corruption as the Old_Italic case: the script name Rejang is detached from its code-point range A930-A946 and appended to a different script's entry on the previous page. A reader or extractor working page by page sees Psalter_Pahlavi's line polluted and Rejang's range unattributed.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides at 300 dpi. PDF page 1018 (printed folio 988), rendered via scripts/spec/page_workunit.py: the final content lines of the body are "Psalter_Pahlavi:" on one line and "10B80-10B91" on the next. Below that is blank space to the bottom margin, then the footer "988 (C)ISO/IEC 2023" and the license watermark. No "Rejang:" token appears anywhere on page 1018 - I looked at the printed glyphs directly, and the line reads exactly "10B80-10B91" with nothing following it. PDF page 1019 (printed folio 989), rendered the same way: the first body line under the running head "ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)" is "Rejang:", and the line directly beneath it is "A930-A946". The name and its range are an intact two-line entry entirely on page 1019, matching the layout of every other entry in this list. Markdown specs/ISO_COBOL.md: line 40610 is "10B80-10B91 Rejang:" - a single line that merges page 1018's last range with page 1019's first script name. Line 40611 is blank, 40612-40614 are the page-1019 furniture (, ## Page 1019, # ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)), 40615 blank, and line 40616 is a bare "A930-A946" with no owning script name. Both halves of the claim are quoted accurately. This is not merely page-break furniture, line wrapping, or hyphenation, and it survives the obvious mitigations: - It is not a reflow of a wrapped line. In the PDF, "10B80-10B91" is a complete line terminated by the page end, and "Rejang:" is a complete line beginning the next page. The markdown line "10B80-10B91 Rejang:" is a line that exists nowhere in the PDF. - It is not recoverable by stripping page furniture. Deleting the /## Page/# ISO-IEC lines still leaves "10B80-10B91 Rejang:" followed by a blank line and then an orphan "A930-A946". Correct recovery requires special-case knowledge that a trailing "Name:" token on a range line means "this name owns the next page's first range" - i.e. the data cannot be parsed by the same rule that parses every other entry in the list. - It does change meaning for this content. The list is a name-to-code-point-range mapping (the Unicode script table in the character-repertoire annex). The transcription asserts a Psalter_Pahlavi entry with a trailing stray token and an unowned range A930-A946, and it places the string "Rejang" on the wrong page. Any entry-scoped or page-scoped extraction yields wrong data. The claimed sibling is also real, which confirms this is a systematic transcription defect rather than a one-off: at the 1017/1018 boundary, line 40558 reads "10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:" and the page-1018 block then opens headless with "10300-1031F, 1032D-1032F" (line 40564). Same shape: the first script name of page N+1 is pulled back onto the last range line of page N. No counter-evidence found. The claim is accurate as written.
verdict.corrected_description:
Confirmed as described; two refinements for the ledger.

(1) Scope/impact calibration. No characters are lost - this is a misplacement plus a line merge, not a deletion. The full token sequence "...10B80-10B91 Rejang: ... A930-A946" is present in file order; what is corrupted is the line structure, the page attribution, and therefore the name-to-range association. Severity "structural" is right; it should not be read as "text missing".

(2) The defect is systematic at page boundaries in this annex, not specific to Rejang. Confirmed instances in the same list: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 40558 "10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:" at the 1017/1018 boundary (page-1018 block then opens headless at line 40564 with "10300-1031F, 1032D-1032F"), and line 40610 "10B80-10B91 Rejang:" at the 1018/1019 boundary (page-1019 block opens headless at line 40616 with "A930-A946"). The pattern is: the first script-name line printed on page N+1 is appended to the last range line of page N's block, leaving page N+1's block starting with an unattributed range. Any fix should sweep the whole annex for the pattern /^[0-9A-F][0-9A-F,\- ]*\s[A-Za-z][A-Za-z_]*:$/ immediately preceding a page marker rather than patching the two known sites.

(3) Note for anyone cross-checking: an unrelated, correctly-transcribed copy of a similar script/range list exists later in the same file (around lines 49358-49409, where "Old_Italic:", "Psalter_Pahlavi:" and "Rejang:" each sit correctly on their own lines with their own ranges). That later block is a different table with different range values and must not be mistaken for evidence that the page-1018 site is fine.
